claims.exact_statement: For every n>=0 and every Boolean D:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}, let K(+1,z)=1, K(-1,z)=D(z), and p=Pr[D=-1]. Then I_x(K)=p, I(K)=I(D)/2+p, and H(K)=H(D)/2+p*c(p), where c(p)=[2(1-p)^2 log_2(1/(1-p))+2p^2 log_2(1/p)+4p(1-p)-(1-2p)^2 log_2(1/|1-2p|)]/p with continuous endpoint conventions. The sharp coefficient C_*=max_{0<=p<=1}c(p) has a unique maximizer p_* in (0.22944127,0.22944128) and satisfies 4.872321<C_*<4.872322. Consequently H(D)<=C I(D) implies H(K)<=max(C,C_*) I(K).
